A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VKRayGS research, with matching main sections and Appendices A–C. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B report original rendering-speed and image-quality evaluations on MipNeRF360 and Tanks&Temples, accompanied by qualitative experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark measurements in Tables 1–2 and qualitative results in Figures 4–8.

M1.justification: Sections 4–5 retain the same 3D quad construction, vertex and fragment shaders, and MIP opacity formulation. No algorithmic component or rendering procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same nine MipNeRF360 and five Tanks&Temples scenes, including the same distant-camera bicycle and close-object room scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains GOF versus VKRayGS, Table 2 retains GS versus VKGS, and Figure 4 retains the MSAA and MIP variants. The newly cited Gumhold work is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 retains the every-eighth-image test split, dataset-specific downsampling, RTX2080 hardware, FPS/PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics, and disabled MIP for quantitative evaluation.

E4.justification: The MIP, MSAA, and opacity-modulation comparisons in Figure 4, close-object artifact examples in Figure 5, and qualitative comparisons in Appendix C retain the same analyses and images.

E5.justification: Both retain averaging over test views. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2 and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports bicycle rendering speeds of 4 FPS for GOF and 177 FPS for VKRayGS in both versions.

T1.justification: Definitions, derivations, and Propositions A.1–A.6 retain their mathematical content. V2 makes the existing μ and Σ arguments explicit in two Section 3.3 expressions and adjusts spacing in Appendix A.1; these are notation and typesetting edits.

C1.justification: Both retain the claims of fast hardware-rasterized RayGS, approximately 40× faster rendering while retaining appearance quality, and MIP-based alias-free rendering. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain their scientific claims.

C2.justification: Discussions of near-plane clipping, MIP approximation limitations, renderer-dependent quality differences, and training-time acceleration as future work remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The Vulkan/VKGS implementation description, code-access link, hardware information, scene-model provenance, and documented rendering settings are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Gumhold’s 2003 work, Splatting illuminated ellipsoids with depth correction, and describes its hardware-rasterization technique as close in spirit to the proposed approach. The remaining cited works are retained, with subsequent references renumbered.

P1.justification: V2 adds one closing related-work sentence and makes limited notation and spacing edits. Section organization and the remaining narrative are unchanged.

P2.justification: First-page title-block spacing and text flow change slightly, and the added reference shifts bibliography breaks. Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–2 retain their content, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves research positioning by acknowledging previously uncited work that it describes as close in spirit, and clarifies existing Gaussian-divergence notation. These are limited gains in contextualization and clarity; the technical contributions, empirical evidence, and limitations otherwise remain unchanged.
